conventions.convention: The base is a field of characteristic different from 2; V is finite-dimensional, B is symmetric bilinear and may be degenerate, and Q(v)=B(v,v).
The plus-Q Clifford convention is used: the canonical generator satisfies v̄²=Q(v)1, and Cl abbreviates Cl⁺.
Exterior multiplication acts on the left; contraction deletes position j with coefficient (-1)^(j-1)B(v,w_j), and contraction annihilates 1.
PBW uses a fixed ordered basis. The word-length filtration starts with F₋₁=0, includes the empty word 1 in F₀, and identifies the exterior algebra with the associated graded algebra.
Simple modules are nonzero modules with no proper nonzero submodules; semisimple modules are direct sums of simple modules. The counterexample concerns the left regular module.

load_bearing.statement: Over a field of characteristic different from 2, for any symmetric bilinear form on an n-dimensional space with fixed ordered basis, 1 and the increasing square-free Clifford monomials form a basis. The dimension is 2^n, and the natural map from the exterior algebra to the word-length associated graded Clifford algebra is a graded algebra isomorphism. No nondegeneracy hypothesis is needed.

For a finite-dimensional vector space over a field of characteristic different from 2 and symmetric bilinear B, put Q(v)=B(v,v). Define Cl⁺(V,Q)=T_k(V)/J_Q, where J_Q is the smallest two-sided ideal containing j(v)²-Q(v)1 for every v. No nondegeneracy assumption is imposed.

For k,V,B,Q as in the Clifford definition and a unital associative k-algebra A, every k-linear f:V→A satisfying f(v)²=Q(v)1_A for all v extends uniquely to a unital k-algebra homomorphism from Cl(V,Q) to A.

For a finite-dimensional vector space over a field of characteristic different from 2 and any symmetric bilinear B, the displayed contraction on decomposable wedges is well defined and k-linear, and c(v)=ε_v+ι_v satisfies c(v)²=Q(v)I.
For k,V,B,Q as in the Clifford definition, v̄w̄+w̄v̄=2B(v,w)1 for all v,w∈V.
A unital k-algebra homomorphism ψ:T_k(V)→A killing every j(v)²-Q(v)1 factors uniquely through a unital k-algebra homomorphism Cl(V,Q)→A.

seams_checked.note: The representation page supplies compatible unital algebra-action context. The Clifford page correctly identifies its exact tensor-algebra suppliers separately; its exterior representation uses composition in End_k(ΛV). Neither side assumes an automatic tensor action.

The spin-factor comparison uses the plus-Q relation, its factor 2 in polarization, and independence of 1 and the degree-one PBW words. Its finite-dimensional real positive-definite hypotheses specialize the supplier hypotheses correctly.

Parity, even-subalgebra, low-dimensional, recurrence, classification, and graded-product consumers preserve the plus-square convention and finite-dimensional universal-property/PBW interfaces. The graded orthogonal-sum theorem retains degenerate forms; the matrix classification explicitly requires nondegeneracy.

The finite-mode comparison uses complex dimension 2n, Q(z)=Σz_r², and anticommutators 2δ_rs. Its Majorana map satisfies the square relation for every linear combination before applying universality, and the inverse formulas have the correct signs. The n=0 case is included.
